activity.notes: Jezebel was a Phoenician princess who married Ahab of the northern Kingdom of Israel and remained a major court figure into the reigns of their sons. Exact absolute chronology varies, so ATLAS uses a broad approximate ninth-century window. Phoenician origin does not create a separate rulership of Canaan or Phoenicia.

sources.title: Jewish Encyclopedia — Ahab
sources.citation_text: The entry dates Ahab's reign to the mid-ninth century BCE and identifies Jezebel as his queen and daughter of Ethbaal, king of Tyre.

sources.title: Encyclopedia.com — Jezebel
sources.citation_text: The reference identifies Jezebel as a ninth-century BCE Phoenician princess who became the wife of Ahab, king of Israel, and was killed during Jehu's coup.

review_context.correction_note: Bind her political role to Israel; treat Phoenicia as dynastic origin, not another sovereign office.
